svg.aria-label: Diagram: Microsoft Entra External ID external tenant configuration compared with a workforce tenant. An external tenant is distinct and separate from the workforce tenant, can only be created from the Microsoft Entra admin center rather than the Azure portal, and provides clear separation between the corporate workforce directory and the customer-facing app directory. By default users created in an external tenant are restricted from accessing information about other users, groups or devices, with default permissions limited to reading and updating their own profile, changing their own password, signing in with a local or social account, accessing applications and revoking consent to applications. What is absent in an external tenant includes Microsoft Entra ID Protection, Microsoft Entra ID Governance, terms of use Conditional Access policies, provisioning logs, cross-tenant synchronization, application proxy, the application gallery catalog, My Apps self-service assignment, application management policies for secrets, and the resource owner password credentials flow. Conditional Access in an external tenant is reduced: assignments include all users with exclusions only, conditions are limited to device platforms and locations with no sign-in risk or user risk, grant controls are limited to block access, require multifactor authentication and require password reset, and session controls are sign-in frequency and persistent browser session. Activity log retention is seven days. What is present only in an external tenant includes native authentication for mobile apps, the OnAttributeCollectionStart, OnAttributeCollectionSubmit and OnOtpSend custom authentication extension events, sign-up logs covering successful and failed sign-ups, and Security Store integrations for sign-up fraud protection with Arkose Labs and HUMAN Security, DDoS and web application firewall protection with Cloudflare and Akamai, and security analytics with Azure Monitor and Microsoft Sentinel. Authentication methods available are email with password for sign-in and sign-up, email one-time passcode for sign-in, sign-up, password reset and multifactor authentication, SMS for multifactor authentication only, passkey FIDO2 for sign-in and multifactor authentication, and Apple, Facebook, Google, Microsoft account, Microsoft Entra ID, OpenID Connect and SAML federation for sign-in and sign-up. Applications in an external tenant are always single tenant, use the authority URL tenant-name.ciamlogin.com, are limited to the Microsoft Graph offline_access, openid and User.Read permissions plus the developer's own APIs, and only the Cloud Application Administrator role applies. Billing is monthly active user pricing for all users regardless of role or user type, whereas a workforce tenant charges MAU only for guests. Azure AD B2C stopped being available to purchase for new customers on 1 May 2025.
svg.title: External ID is not Entra ID with customers in it: a separate product sharing a platform
svg.text: Same platform, different product. The premium half is removed; a consumer half is added.
“An external tenant provides clear separation between your corporate workforce directory and your customer-facing app directory.”
And at last, a default that is tight rather than generous
“By default, users created in your external tenant are restricted from accessing information about other users, groups, or
devices in the external tenant.” Five permitted actions: read and update own profile · change own password · sign in with
a local or social account · access applications · revoke consent to applications. Ten writable profile properties.
Not available in an external tenant
no risk detections, so no risk-based policy at all
no access reviews, no entitlement management
App gallery catalog · My Apps · application proxy
Resource owner password credentials (use native auth)
App management policies for secrets and certificates
“During the preview, features… that require a premium
license are unavailable in external tenants.”
Available ONLY in an external tenant
your own screens — but no cross-app SSO via browsers
Fraud and edge protection, wired in
Arkose Labs · HUMAN Security — sign-up fraud and bots
The Security Store wizard is NOT in workforce tenants.
Conditional Access is a smaller engine here, and “supported” hides it
— no risk signals exist to key on
Every policy is tenant-wide by construction, with holes punched in it — the inverse of the scope-narrowly habit from post #41a.
The method matrix: one backbone, and two asymmetries
Apple · Facebook · Google · MSA · Entra · OIDC · SAML
Email OTP is the only method at all four stages, so it is the backbone whether you planned it or not. SMS cannot carry sign-in.
Passkeys cannot carry sign-up, so enrolment happens after the account exists.
The number most likely to cause a problem
Activity log retention in an external tenant: SEVEN DAYS. Azure Monitor export for external tenants is still preview.
So exporting is day-one work. Also: apps are always single-tenant, authority is tenant-name.ciamlogin.com, Graph is limited to
offline_access, openid and User.Read, and MAU bills every user — “regardless of role or UserType value”.
